federalism.title: Senate divisions
federalism.citation: Constitution Act, 1867, s. 22 (four divisions of 24 senators, with Newfoundland and the territories added)
federalism.detail: The Senate is built from four equal divisions of provinces. A region that spans two divisions has no seat count that follows from the text. 8 regions span two or more divisions: St. John's, Charlottetown, Fredericton, Québec, Winnipeg.

federalism.title: The 7/50 amending formula
federalism.citation: Constitution Act, 1982, s. 38(1) (resolutions of two-thirds of the provinces with at least half the population)
federalism.detail: Two-thirds of the units, holding at least half the population, can amend the constitution. With a different number of units, the threshold is a different set of people. Two-thirds of 14 units is 10. The 10 largest hold 98% of the people; the 10 smallest hold 21%.

federalism.title: Equalization
federalism.citation: Constitution Act, 1982, s. 36(2) (equalization payments so provinces can provide reasonably comparable services at reasonably comparable levels of taxation)
federalism.detail: Equalization measures fiscal capacity per person against the national average. Redrawing the units moves the average and changes who is below it. 8 of 14 regions fall below the set's GDP per person; Charlottetown is furthest below it. GDP here is an allocation, so read this as a shape, not a payment.

federalism.title: Quebec's asymmetry
federalism.citation: Constitution Act, 1867, ss. 94, 133 and Constitution Act, 1982, s. 59 (Quebec's civil law, its legislature and its language guarantees)
federalism.detail: Quebec's civil law, language guarantees and opt-outs attach to Quebec as a unit. A set that cuts Quebec into pieces has to say which piece they attach to. Quebec is spread over 5 regions, and 5 of them also hold ground in another province.

federalism.title: Territorial status
federalism.citation: Northwest Territories Act, S.C. 2014, c. 2, s. 2; Yukon Act, S.C. 2002, c. 7; Nunavut Act, S.C. 1993, c. 28 (territories are created by Parliament, not by the constitutional amending formula)
federalism.detail: The territories exist by federal statute and can be changed by Parliament alone; provinces cannot. A region joining territory to province mixes the two. 4 regions join territory to province: Québec, Whitehorse, Yellowknife, Ottawa.

federalism.title: The senatorial floor on Commons seats
federalism.citation: Constitution Act, 1867, s. 51A (no province has fewer Commons seats than senators)
federalism.detail: The floor keeps small provinces over-represented in the Commons. It is written for provinces as they are; new units of very different size change who it protects. The smallest region holds 0.0% of the set's people, under one seat's worth, so the floor would carry it.
